ROBERT DOLLARD (Republican) was born in
Fall River, Massachusetts, on March 14, 1842.
A member of Company B of the Fourth Regiment,
Massachusetts Volunteer Militia, his command
comprised a part of the Minutemen of Massa-
chusetts. The first to respond to the call
for troops at the outbreak of the war,
Dollard attained the rank of major by the
close of the war. He was admitted to the bar
in May 1870 in Illinois and in 1879 he moved
to Douglas County, Dakota. The records of the
United States land office show him to be the
first settler in the county. Major Dollard
was a Republican and by that party was
elected to several important offices. He was
a leading member of the state constitutional
convention in 1883 and 1885. Unanimously he
was elected district attorney of Bon Homme
County in 1884. Mr. Dollard was elected at-
torney general under the provisional state
government in 1885 and a prominent member of
the council of the territorial Legislature in
1888. In 1889 Robert was elected the first
attorney general of the state of South Dakota
and was reelected the next year. In 1892 he
was elected to the state Senate and in 1896
was elected to the House; Dollard represented
Bon Home County each term. On September 29,
1875, he married Miss Carrie E. Dunn. Dollard
passed away in 1912.
